question: A 16-year-old teenager is brought to the emergency department after having slipped on ice while walking to school. She hit her head on the side of the pavement and retained consciousness. She was brought to the closest ER within an hour of the incident. The ER physician sends her immediately to get a CT scan and also orders routine blood work. The physician understands that in cases of stress, such as in this patient, the concentration of certain hormones will be increased, while others will be decreased. Considering allosteric regulation by hormones, which of the following enzymes will most likely be inhibited in this patient?

enhanced_information: In response to stress, the body activates the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, leading to increased levels of cortisol and epinephrine. Cortisol promotes gluconeogenesis and inhibits insulin secretion, which can lead to increased blood glucose levels. Pyruvate carboxylase, which is involved in gluconeogenesis, is generally activated under these conditions, not inhibited. Conversely, phosphofructokinase (PFK), a key regulatory enzyme in glycolysis, is inhibited by high levels of cortisol and glucagon, as the body prioritizes gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis during stress. Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase is activated during gluconeogenesis, not inhibited. Glycogen phosphorylase is activated to promote glycogen breakdown, not inhibited. Therefore, the most likely enzyme to be inhibited in this patient due to the stress response is phosphofructokinase, aligning with the consensus on metabolic regulation during stress.
